title: Ctrl+Alt+Timeline
blurb: Your feed, your playlist, your paycheck, and the plot twists behind all three.

cards.say: Netflix [turned down an offer of about 15 million dollars from Amazon in 1998], [tried to sell itself to Blockbuster for 50 million dollars in 2000], [mailed out VHS tapes until it switched to DVDs in 1999], and [mailed out its very last rental DVD in 2023].
cards.real: Netflix never rented VHS. Tapes were too bulky to mail cheaply, so it shipped DVDs from the start.
src: https://techcrunch.com/2023/04/22/netflix-history-25-years/amp/ (Amazon was interested to the tune of 15 million dollars)
https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Timeline_of_Netflix (2000: offered itself to Blockbuster for 50 million dollars)
https://techcrunch.com/2023/04/22/netflix-history-25-years/amp/ (VHS tapes too bulky to mail; DVDs instead)
https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Timeline_of_Netflix (last shipment September 29, 2023)

cards.say: Vine [was shut down by Twitter in January 2015], [was bought by Twitter for 30 million dollars in 2012], [started testing videos longer than six seconds in 2016], and [had several of its stars move into one apartment complex on Vine Street].
cards.real: Twitter announced Vine's end in October 2016, and it shut down in January 2017, about four years after it launched.
src: https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/look-back-vine-six-second-video-app-made-us-scream-laugh-cry-rcna10910 (shutdown announced October 2016, folded January 18, 2017); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service) (launched January 24, 2013, shut down January 17, 2017)

https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/look-back-vine-six-second-video-app-made-us-scream-laugh-cry-rcna10910 (acquired by Twitter in October 2012 for 30 million dollars); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_(service) (June 2016: testing clips up to 140 seconds); https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/look-back-vine-six-second-video-app-made-us-scream-laugh-cry-rcna10910 (broke away from its six-second rule in 2016)

https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/look-back-vine-six-second-video-app-made-us-scream-laugh-cry-rcna10910 (around 2014, a number of Vine stars moved into an apartment complex on Vine Street)

cards.say: Rickrolling [got Rick Astley voted Best Act Ever at the 2008 MTV Europe Music Awards], [put Rick Astley on a float in the 2008 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade], [was pulled by the White House's own Twitter account in 2011], and [began in 2007 as a fake link to a Halo 3 trailer].
cards.real: The first rickroll, in May 2007, was a link dressed up as a trailer for Grand Theft Auto IV.

cards.say: Bitcoin [was first described in a paper posted on Halloween 2008], [had its very first block mined on New Year's Day 2009], [hid a London newspaper headline inside its very first block], and [was used to buy two pizzas for 10,000 bitcoins in 2010].
cards.real: The first block was mined on January 3, 2009, with a headline from that day's Times of London tucked inside.

cards.say: Twitter [got the hashtag from its own founders in 2007], [bought its first bird logo from a stock image site for under 20 dollars], [saw its cofounder's first tweet sell as an NFT for about 2.9 million dollars], and [didn't make hashtags clickable until 2009].
cards.real: Blogger Chris Messina proposed the hashtag in an August 2007 tweet, and Twitter didn't adopt it right away.

cards.say: Instagram [had 13 employees when Facebook bought it for a billion dollars], [didn't come out for Android phones until 2012], [started out under the name Picaboo], and [had its own CEO say Snapchat deserved all the credit for Stories].
cards.real: Picaboo was Snapchat's original name in 2011. Instagram launched as Instagram, on the iPhone, in October 2010.
src: https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2012/4/10/facebook-updates-status-with-instagram-deal (1 billion dollars, 13 employees)

cards.say: Myspace [was the most visited website in the US in 2006], [was co-founded by Justin Timberlake in 2003], [sold for 35 million dollars, six years after selling for 580 million], and [lost more than 50 million uploaded songs in a server move].
cards.real: Tom Anderson and Chris DeWolfe created Myspace in 2003. Justin Timberlake came in as a part-owner in 2011.
src: https://www.npr.org/2019/03/18/704458168/myspace-says-it-lost-years-of-user-uploaded-music (in 2006 MySpace was the most visited site in the US)

https://www.npr.org/2019/03/18/704458168/myspace-says-it-lost-years-of-user-uploaded-music (more than 50 million tracks lost in a server migration)

cards.say: Slack [was bought by Microsoft for 27.7 billion dollars], [began as a chat tool inside a company making an online game], [is named for Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge], and [signed up 8,000 customers in its first day].
cards.real: Salesforce bought Slack for about 27.7 billion dollars. The deal was announced in December 2020 and closed in July 2021.

cards.say: The Return of the King [won every one of the 11 Oscars it was up for], [won Best Picture without a single acting nomination], [was the second movie ever to make a billion dollars], and [was the first sequel ever to win Best Picture].
cards.real: The Godfather Part II was the first sequel to win Best Picture, for 1974. The Return of the King was the second, 29 years later.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/76th_Academy_Awards (a clean sweep of its eleven nominations)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/76th_Academy_Awards (the tenth Best Picture winner without any acting nominations)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series) (only the second sequel to win Best Picture, after The Godfather Part II)

cards.say: Stranger Things [was first pitched under the title Montauk], [was filmed in Indiana, where its town of Hawkins is set], [was turned down by more than a dozen networks before Netflix], and [had more than 1,200 kids audition using scenes from Stand by Me].
cards.real: Hawkins, Indiana is made up. Most of the show was filmed in Georgia, with the small town of Jackson standing in for Hawkins.
src: https://www.mentalfloss.com/entertainment/stranger-things/facts-about-stranger-things-netflix (initially called Montauk)
https://www.afar.com/magazine/stranger-things-filming-locations-in-georgia (most of the series filmed in Georgia; downtown Jackson stands in for Hawkins)
https://www.mentalfloss.com/entertainment/stranger-things/several-networks-passed-on-netflix-stranger-things (Matt Duffer to Rolling Stone: rejected by 15 to 20 networks)
https://www.mentalfloss.com/entertainment/stranger-things/facts-about-stranger-things-netflix (1,213 child actors read pilot scenes and scenes from Stand By Me)

cards.say: Blockbuster [had about 9,000 stores at its peak], [didn't offer online rentals until 2004], [was down to one last store, in Alaska, by 2019], and [ended up with a last store that opened in 1992 as Pacific Video].
cards.real: In 2019 the last Blockbuster on Earth was the one in Bend, Oregon.
